reservoir_ep07_001.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_001.text: On the morning after the grain commission ended, Yue paid for her own breakfast. The receiving house had not changed its smell overnight: millet steam still climbed the dark rafters, and a girl at the next table still complained that the pickles were too sour. What had changed was the hand that met the bill. Yue placed two coppers beside the bowl and room token. The ten she had reserved would cover these five days. She ate slowly enough to notice that freedom could have an ordinary price.

reservoir_ep07_002.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_002.text: Tian brought the repaired basket past her table, now lined with an old sleeve. He had decided that anything capable of flying six paces deserved warmer clothing. Yue suggested it had merely wanted a better view of the gardener's cabbages. Tian replied that its next voyage would require a written invitation. Their laughter drew the girl's attention away from the pickles. She asked whether the basket really flew, and Tian admitted that the wind had done every useful part while he lay on the floor.

reservoir_ep07_003.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_003.text: That afternoon Yue walked to the lower public footbridge. Below it, water slid between two stones whose upper faces remained dry even after yesterday's rain. She had spent weeks hearing people describe this basin through schedules, quantities and disputed marks. Its actual voice was less orderly. A loose reed struck the bridge support at unequal intervals. A duck fought another duck for an unremarkable patch of water. Yue leaned on neither rail with her injured shoulder and watched until the quarrel moved beyond hearing.

reservoir_ep07_004.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_004.text: Fu found her there with a bundle of repaired flour cloths. The household trial had returned to its ordinary receivers; neither woman needed to spend this afternoon repeating its records. Fu wanted help remembering the second line of the song sung at Zhou's birthday. Yue remembered three incompatible versions and sang the worst. Fu laughed, then supplied a fourth. They agreed that the singer had probably forgotten the original himself. The cloth bundle was light, but Fu kept it. Yue's company was welcome without requiring another borrowed task.

reservoir_ep07_005.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_005.text: On Day One Thousand Seventy-six, Yue washed her own bedding at the receiving house's ordinary trough. The cold water made her fingers blunt. A woman beside her worked soap into a child's sleeve while telling the child, who was nowhere nearby, exactly what she would say when she caught him. Yue held her sleeve against the trough wall and scrubbed below waist height. She could use her arm within that familiar range. A cultivation title would not make the higher rail a sensible place to wring it.

reservoir_ep07_006.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_006.text: The trough woman introduced herself as a seller of bean cakes and asked whether Yue intended to stay. Yue said she had requested a place to study, but no receiving decision had arrived. The woman considered that uncertainty and offered the last cake in her basket at its usual price. Yue bought it from her own remaining food allowance. They shared no revelation. The cake was warm at its center, and the woman wanted to leave before her troublesome grandson found another puddle. Yue wished her success.

reservoir_ep07_007.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_007.text: Jing was sorting returned sample sleeves when Yue visited the public desk on the following day. None belonged to Yue; none had come from the closed city appointment. Jing had found a split seam in one sleeve and set it aside before counting the usable stock. Yue asked whether every crack was visible. Jing said the difficult ones often announced themselves through somebody's beautiful result. She would rather discover a disappointing container before a candidate discovered an impressive number that depended upon its leak.

reservoir_ep07_008.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_008.text: Yue offered to carry the rejected sleeve to the ordinary repair shelf. Jing accepted that small task and gave her the shelf's exact location. They passed a boy trying to balance an empty cup on his nose. Jing waited until the cup fell harmlessly into his lap before telling him its owner needed it for tea. The boy explained that he was practicing concentration. Jing said that remembering whose cup he had borrowed would be a useful beginning. Yue carried the sleeve without laughing until they reached the shelf.

reservoir_ep07_009.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_009.text: Qiu delivered the receiving appointment for Day One Thousand Seventy-eight herself. She did not offer it as a reward for the water calendar work. The new teaching allocation had arrived from three named sources, and the ordinary board had selected a candidate place under its published conditions. Yue could accept those conditions or decline the place. Qiu wanted her to read them before the meeting, especially the provisions for failed attempts and absences. Yue took the folded paper to her room and spread it beside her private family letter.

reservoir_ep07_010.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_010.text: The letter was no examination document. Her mother had added a small crooked drawing of the kiln yard's plum tree, whose lowest branch now leaned farther toward the wall. Beside it she had written that somebody should remind the tree it owned no land beyond the boundary. Yue traced the drawing with a clean finger. The woman who had written it still lived with the cost of the old bargain. Her humor had survived beside that cost, and Yue refused to turn either fact into proof that the other had disappeared.

reservoir_ep07_011.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_011.text: At the receiving meeting, Mei Rong sat opposite the teaching board's clerk. Her square bronze reading glass rested on a cord against her slate robe. She asked Yue to describe the interruption that remained hardest to handle. Yue began with a practiced account of her small circuit, then stopped. The truthful answer was sudden noise after a bad night, when she wanted to finish one more sequence before releasing. Mei wrote that answer down. A polished description would not help either woman decide which conditions actually needed testing.

reservoir_ep07_012.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_012.text: The board's received purse held eight hundred eighty coppers. Four hundred eighty came from the teaching trust, two hundred forty from the regional work-study guild, and one hundred sixty from the basin's separate training fund. Qiu placed the three acknowledgments where Yue could read them. The old household water fund and completed grain commission contributed nothing to this purse. Their work had ended on their own terms. This new allocation bought a finite course beginning on Day One Thousand Eighty and ending on Day One Thousand Three Hundred Fifty-nine.

reservoir_ep07_013.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_013.text: Food and a modest bed occupied five hundred sixty coppers of the course ceiling, two for each of its two hundred eighty calendar days. One paid for the reserved bed, one for actual ordinary meals. A family absence could leave the bed held while unused meal money returned to the source allocation; it could not become private travel cash. Yue was glad somebody had said that before she booked a road. She had lived long enough among good intentions to know how easily the same copper could acquire two imaginary duties.

reservoir_ep07_014.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_014.text: Seventy-two coppers paid Mei's independent examination work. The amount did not rise if Yue passed or disappear if she failed. Mei answered to the agreed examination record rather than the lesson giver. Eighteen paid Jing's instrument custody, and another eighteen paid licensed instruction in the small circuit Yue had already earned. The qualified instructor, Deng Yi, was not present to sell an advancement promise. His first duty would be to observe her ordinary practice and correct its existing faults within the range already tested.

reservoir_ep07_015.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_015.text: Fifty-two coppers reserved planned materials. Twelve more reserved three ordinary clinical checks on the mornings after the eventual qualifying trials, four for each actual appointment. Ninety-six funded thirty-two eight-hour equivalents of ordinary course work at three coppers each, payable for completed duties. These were wages, not gifts for trying hard. The final fifty-two formed a separate recovery reserve. Yue read the division twice. Together the lines exhausted the eight hundred eighty without making a future pass pay for a present meal or a clinician's missing time.

reservoir_ep07_016.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_016.text: The recovery reserve was concrete enough to make Yue uneasy. Sixteen covered four ordinary post-failure clinical appointments. Twenty-four covered eight protected rest days at three coppers, and twelve covered replacement materials consumed by failed attempts. Mei explained that a stopped test could damage confidence without damaging tissue, or do both. The examiner needed to be able to stop it either way. Protected recovery bought the actual time and care to return safely. It was not a consolation prize that could be withdrawn because the candidate looked cheerful afterward.

reservoir_ep07_017.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_017.text: Yue asked what would happen if the reserve proved insufficient. Qiu said the next attempt would wait for a new funded decision; no worker had agreed to vanish into unpaid service. That answer disappointed Yue more than she wanted it to. She had hoped a careful plan might mean the difficult future was already contained. Mei noticed the tightening of her hand around the paper. She told Yue to leave that hope outside the measurement room. A plan could make failure survivable without making failure obey the plan.

reservoir_ep07_018.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_018.text: Deng Yi arrived carrying his own worn stool, because the teaching room's high bench aggravated his knee. He was an ordinary qualified instructor whose license named the small-circuit methods he could supervise. He greeted Mei with the practiced courtesy of colleagues who sometimes disagreed. They discussed the interruption Yue had described, then asked her to show a grounded release without drawing more input. She sat on the low mat and let the familiar circuit settle. The stool creaked when Deng shifted his weight. Yue kept her breath ordinary.

reservoir_exam_prior_practice.speaker: narrator
reservoir_exam_prior_practice.text: The first observation did not raise her stage. Deng saw a late release after the second interruption and asked her to repeat the stop at lower demand. He did not ask for a stronger draw to demonstrate resolve. Yue tried again while Jing closed a shutter softly, then while she closed it with its usual wooden knock. The second sound startled Yue's neck. She completed the release nevertheless, and admitted that she had been bracing against a third noise. Deng marked the anticipation as something they could practice separately.

reservoir_ep07_020.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_020.text: After the meeting Yue found Tian outside balancing three bean cakes in the basket. He offered one and asked whether she had become impressive yet. She said she had been told to stop more accurately. Tian considered this a useful qualification for anybody living near their unreliable shutter. He had made the cakes himself and one was almost round. Yue chose the crooked one because it held more filling. His pride in that plain advantage made her happier than an undeserved compliment about a realm she had not reached.

reservoir_ep07_021.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_021.text: On Day One Thousand Seventy-nine, she paid the last of the five private bed and food days. The reserved ten coppers were gone for their stated purpose. Thirty-seven of her completed grain wages remained separate from the course fund, with her earlier unspent travel contingency in its own fold. She did not merge the purses merely because all their coins looked alike. Then she put the account away and used the remaining daylight to mend a loose hem. Tomorrow's lesson would be easier without a trailing thread beneath her heel.

reservoir_ep07_022.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_022.text: The course began at the low practice pavilion on Day One Thousand Eighty. Rain had loosened a patch of earth beside its door, and somebody had laid a board across it. Yue crossed at walking speed. Inside, Jing showed her a clean empty sleeve and its paired blank before any input entered the comparison. Deng placed the low stool where she could see the door without turning her shoulder. Mei attended the registration of standards, then left the ordinary instruction to its named teacher. Her absence would not make his approval equivalent to hers.

reservoir_ep07_023.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_023.text: The local balanced-reservoir examination required at least seventy-two actually usable qi units after sampling, scheduled work and sleep. The independently compared usable portion had to show at least ninety-two percent compatibility. Temperature change, ordinary movement and interrupted sleep each demanded a separately recovered qualifying trial, followed by its own next-day check. These were this board's preregistered conditions for certifying its stage-eight practice. Mei had stated them before the first difficult attempt. Yue could not meet a lower number and ask them to rename her disappointment as attainment.

reservoir_ep07_024.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_024.text: Seventy-two was not a number Yue could borrow from a future claim. Her last earned small circuit remained stage seven, and no certificate from the city described today's reserve. Deng explained that usable quantity could decline during work, sampling or a poor night's rest. A remembered peak was a memory of a condition, not an inventory she still held. Their first task was to measure the body that had actually arrived. Yue found the distinction harder to accept than the arithmetic. The person she wanted to be kept reaching forward for somebody else's result.

reservoir_ep07_025.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_025.text: The physical application ceiling remained one eighth of a unit per ordinary breath, with no more than half a unit of input across the familiar four-breath task. Its already measured useful output was a quarter unit. Nothing in the new reserve criterion authorized a greater draw, a longer range or an overhead shoulder catch. Deng asked her to demonstrate the release again before he mentioned storage. Yue did so on the low mat. Water drummed on the roof, but he waited until she had finished before moving his stool.

reservoir_ep07_026.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_026.text: The registration also named full grounding, ordinary stop signals and separate clearance for unfamiliar loads. Yue understood those words through the scarred history of her shoulder rather than through a fear of paperwork. She remembered the shutter's sudden pull and how little time there had been to choose a safe range. Keeping the familiar range had allowed her to help Tian once. Wanting to help him more could have injured them both. She wrote the remembered circumstance beside the limit, where it would remain recognizable when a flattering situation arrived.

reservoir_ep07_027.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_027.text: On the first evening, the course kitchen served squash broth with a hard end of bread. Yue sat beside another candidate who hated squash so thoroughly that she separated every piece before eating the broth. They traded one piece for half an onion. The other woman wanted to teach canal measurements in her village; Yue wanted a reservoir that survived an ordinary interrupted night. Neither ambition made the meal elegant. By the time they had finished arranging the exchange, both bowls were cold and they were laughing at their own negotiations.

reservoir_ep07_028.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_028.text: Yue woke on Day One Thousand Eighty-one before the kitchen bell. She had dreamed that the basin's ducks were examining her and had rejected her handwriting. The dream left her irritated until she saw Jing carrying a tray of empty sleeves through the yard. Jing said a duck would be a difficult examiner because it would eat the evidence. Yue helped hold the low door open, then went to her assigned preparation. An ordinary joke had removed no obligation, but it made the morning feel less like a sentence awaiting judgment.

reservoir_ep07_029.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_029.text: Deng's second short instructional session worked on the pause between intake and a chosen stop. He asked Yue to speak a simple sentence before beginning, so the practice belonged to a person still able to attend to the room. She chose to describe the soup trade. At the second pause he asked which vegetable she had received. She answered incorrectly, stopped, and laughed. Her qi did not need to punish an embarrassed mind. They reduced the demand and practiced attending to the real question before beginning another safe sequence.

reservoir_ep07_030.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_030.text: Fu came after the lesson to ask whether Yue would join a planting supper later that week. Yue checked the posted ordinary work day rather than promising while excited. Her first course duty fell on Day One Thousand Eighty-two, an eight-hour equivalent of checking dry grain measures under Zhou's ordinary supervision. The supper would begin afterward and required no extra water testimony. Fu said she was invited to eat, not to record anybody. Yue accepted. The distinction reached her more warmly than the kitchen's squash broth had done.

reservoir_ep07_031.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_031.text: The dry-measure room smelled of old wood rather than damp sacks. Zhou set two ordinary measures on the table and asked Yue to compare their rims before weighing any grain. One had swollen during the previous wet season. A careless full scoop could still look correct while holding a different volume. Yue marked the difference in the accepted work sheet, then let Zhou repeat the comparison. He approved the result because he had checked it, not because a candidate's reserve might one day become larger than his own.

reservoir_ep07_032.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_032.text: At midday Tian arrived with a pot of beans for the workers. He had learned that hot beans carried in the famous basket required an actual lined container. Zhou asked whether the basket had signed an agreement not to depart. Tian said it had demanded more interesting cargo. Yue held the pot at the table while Tian removed its wrapping. The youngest worker burned his tongue after ignoring three warnings, and blamed nobody except the beans. Their meal break ended when the posted bell rang, with ordinary work still waiting.

reservoir_ep07_033.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_033.text: That afternoon a storeroom customer argued that a more cultivated worker should finish the measure comparison twice as fast. Zhou answered by inviting him to show which physical check could safely be omitted. The customer named none, but insisted that Yue looked capable. Yue nearly accepted the compliment as an obligation. Then she noticed the swollen rim beneath her thumb. She told him the same comparison needed the same observed checks whoever held the measure. His disappointment remained his own while she completed the next accepted pair.

reservoir_ep07_034.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_034.text: The customer returned after an hour with a daughter carrying the disputed empty grain bowl. Her family had been receiving a little less than its expected measure, and impatience had hidden the useful question inside his accusation. Yue invited Zhou to examine the bowl's lip against the corrected reference. Its rim was sound. The difference belonged to the store measure, whose seasonal swelling had enlarged the charge. The ordinary receiving correction reduced the charge rather than pretending the family should be grateful for an impressive worker's faster apology.

reservoir_ep07_035.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_035.text: Zhou arranged the actual corrected bill through the storage receiver, separate from the course wage allocation. The customer paid the proper amount and took the grain away. His daughter thanked Yue before he could complain again. Yue had no desire to turn that small thank-you into a lesson about the whole basin. She was relieved they had found the source in time. The swollen measure went to the repair shelf, where its altered rim would trouble nobody until an ordinary worker had checked its returned shape.

reservoir_ep07_036.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_036.text: At the end of the accepted eight-hour equivalent, Zhou signed Yue's three-copper wage. She had completed ordinary work within its declared range, including the repeated measure comparison and supported customer correction. The three went into her personal purse after actual payment. They did not increase a reserve reading or buy examiner approval. On the path to supper she caught herself rehearsing how to tell her mother about the swollen rim. It sounded small beside the story of a realm, yet it had changed one family's bill.

reservoir_ep07_037.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_037.text: Fu's planting supper took place in a courtyard whose bean supports were still empty. Somebody had hung paper fish beneath the trellis, and the weakest fish folded in the damp. Yue sat on an upturned crate because the higher bench would press her shoulder against the wall. Liu arrived with bread whose middle was excellent and whose end was frankly burnt. He cut the burnt end for himself and announced that he had chosen a stronger flavor. Nobody believed him, but the children asked for small black pieces anyway.

reservoir_ep07_038.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_038.text: Jing brought her father, who had retired from pump work and wanted to discuss beans. He disliked being introduced through his old occupation. When Qiu asked whether the beans would tolerate the wet lower corner, he became animated and explained three things nobody should do with that soil. Yue listened without trying to connect his advice to qi compatibility. The best place for the useful knowledge was the garden itself. He asked her to pass the onion dish, and she did, keeping its modest weight close to her waist.

reservoir_ep07_039.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_039.text: Near dusk Fu's brother sang the missing birthday verse with great confidence. It contradicted all four versions the women remembered. He insisted that everyone else had learned it from careless singers. Tian asked whether its final rhyme had always been 'basket.' Fu's brother considered that question and accused him of corrupting ancient songs. Yue laughed until the courtyard's small lamp blurred. For once her attention moved toward the next line because she wanted to hear it, not because she feared an interruption would expose some fault within her.

reservoir_ep07_040.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_040.text: The rain began before the supper ended. Everybody moved bowls beneath the covered walkway, and the paper fish were left to their separate wet destinies. A child tried to rescue the weakest one with a broom. Fu lowered it for her and refused the broom's unnecessary flourish. Yue gathered the plates already within her safe reach; Liu took the high string. Their easy division of tasks did not require a speech about limits. Nobody's pride suffered because the person standing nearest an ordinary ladder climbed it.

reservoir_ep07_041.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_041.text: After supper Qiu walked beside Yue as far as the course gate. She said that the first failed attempts were often socially awkward before they were physically difficult. People who enjoyed a candidate's company might start expecting to celebrate every result. Yue admitted that she had already imagined bringing good news back to the courtyard. Qiu told her to bring news she could stand beside the following morning. The beans and burnt bread would not demand a certificate before another invitation. Yue wanted to believe her and knew she must test that belief.

reservoir_ep07_042.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_042.text: On Day One Thousand Eighty-three, Deng showed her how a familiar four-breath application changed when its start followed an ordinary interruption. He used no new load and no greater range. Yue released correctly twice, then delayed the third stop because she thought his hand movement announced another instruction. He had merely reached for his tea. They separated the visible movement from the agreed signal and repeated at lower demand. Her mistake had been small enough to examine safely. Deng would not make it dramatic by increasing the draw.

reservoir_ep07_043.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_043.text: Jing's custody record distinguished the instrument sleeve, the ordinary blank and the material that a candidate consumed. Yue asked why the blank did not simply count as zero. Jing poured ordinary clean water into two apparently identical cups. One left a faint taste because somebody had stored onion in it. Yue understood the point before Jing completed the analogy. A clean-looking comparison could carry its own history. The blank had to be observed, not wished clean, and its consumed material would be charged to the correct new allocation.

reservoir_ep07_044.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_044.text: Another candidate arrived while Jing was speaking and announced that his uncle had measured an astonishing reserve without any blank. Jing asked whether the uncle's method had an independently comparable reference. The candidate replied that the uncle was respected. Yue looked at the onion cup. Respect might explain why people listened; it could not tell them what the cup added. She said as much quietly. The candidate frowned, then asked Jing to show the ordinary preparation again. His willingness to ask was more promising than his first impressive number.

reservoir_ep07_045.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_045.text: Mei visited the practice pavilion on Day One Thousand Eighty-four to hear the candidates repeat the criteria in their own words. Yue stated the usable quantity after sampling, work and sleep, then the compatibility requirement and the three changed conditions with next-day checks. Mei asked whether a single excellent rested result could replace the interrupted-sleep trial. Yue said it could not. Saying that aloud made the missed shortcut feel sharper. Mei accepted the answer without praising her for surrendering a shortcut the examination had never offered.

reservoir_ep07_046.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_046.text: One candidate objected that interrupted sleep was an unfair condition for an examination. His village had noisy pumps beside every bed. Mei asked whether he wanted a certificate that described a quiet room his village could not provide. He grew angry, then quieter. She did not ask him to consent to damaging exhaustion. The interruption would be ordinary, bounded and stopped if recovery failed. Yue watched the change in his face when unfairness became a question about the life he actually meant to return to afterward.

reservoir_ep07_047.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_047.text: The candidates discussed their sleep outside the pavilion. The man from the pump village had learned to rest through a regular squeak but woke whenever it stopped. Yue understood that inverted alarm. For her, sudden silence after a crowd could feel like the intake before danger. They exchanged descriptions without claiming identical bodies. He asked if she knew a way to prevent it. She said she knew a way to admit it before testing, which was smaller and presently true. He laughed at the size of her answer.

reservoir_ep07_048.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_048.text: That night the course bed felt unfamiliar again. Yue listened to somebody coughing in the next room and remembered her mother's limited shoulder movements beside the kiln. The new allocation bought a finite bed and meals, not an escape from affection. She could not know whether her mother slept comfortably tonight. The last report described an ordinary review and continuing work limits. She folded that report beside the plum-tree drawing. Neither paper changed during the night, and she resisted rereading them as if a fifth reading could become a new reply.

reservoir_ep07_049.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_049.text: Day One Thousand Eighty-five began with an ordinary walk around the practice court. Deng asked Yue to notice where she turned too abruptly because she wanted to keep him in view. He stood still while she repeated the route with her shoulder relaxed and her eyes moving first. They did not add qi to a movement whose ordinary mechanics remained awkward. The ground held a shallow puddle at the corner. Yue stepped around it and discovered she had been inventing an unnecessary sharp turn rather than using the wider path.

reservoir_ep07_050.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_050.text: The practice reminded her of the road decision that had brought her here. Each chosen journey had provided something real and left something else beyond its dates. Neither could be improved by recounting it more gracefully. This wider ordinary turn was still available because she had not committed herself to the puddle. She used it again. Deng watched her feet rather than her expression, then said that the better route had reduced demand on the shoulder. A useful change had occurred before she drew a single additional unit.

reservoir_ep07_051.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_051.text: Jing interrupted them to report that a sample sleeve from the ordinary stock had failed its pressure check. It would not be used for Yue's coming baseline. The replacement belonged to the planned material ceiling and would be issued only after its own accepted check. Yue felt a surprising irritation at the delay. She had waited through city closure and private living days; now she wanted the first measurement to arrive promptly. Deng let her name the irritation. Then he asked whether a faster unreliable result would shorten anything useful.

reservoir_ep07_052.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_052.text: The failed sleeve went back to the repair shelf beside the swollen grain measure. Tian happened to be carrying another cracked cup there. He suggested they might establish a very successful school for imperfect containers. Jing answered that the school already existed and was called the repair shelf. Yue imagined the three objects sitting in solemn rows. The thought made her laugh, then made her kinder toward her own unfinished practice. Being unready for the next load did not require pretending she had never been useful at the previous one.

reservoir_ep07_053.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_053.text: On Day One Thousand Eighty-six, the replacement sleeve passed its ordinary preparation checks. Jing recorded its starting condition and kept the paired blank distinct. She had not yet sampled Yue's usable reserve; the first independently compared baseline belonged to the coming schedule. Yue handled only the permitted ordinary cup beside the table. Its rim was low enough to reach without strain. The low placement was deliberate, and she could see how several people had arranged the room so that an impressive title would never be needed to rescue a falling instrument.

reservoir_ep07_054.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_054.text: Mei returned with the preregistered schedule: a warm-and-cold comparison on Day One Thousand One Hundred, an ordinary movement condition on Day One Thousand One Hundred Four, and changed sleep on Day One Thousand One Hundred Eight. These first attempts might fail. They would proceed only when the previous check permitted the next bounded task. Their dates did not promise three passes, and none could certify stage eight without the later recovered series and its independent follow-up. Yue signed beneath the criteria already read aloud. Now the difficult mornings had names.

reservoir_ep07_055.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_055.text: Deng asked which scheduled condition frightened her most. Yue chose changed sleep. Temperature sounded like a thing on the outside of the room, and movement like a thing she might practice, but sleep belonged to the hours when she could not supervise herself. Deng pointed out that all three would reach the same body. Her distinction was emotionally useful without being a physiological measurement. They began a modest stop practice while the court outside warmed in the afternoon sun. Yue had to release before discussing what her fear might mean.

reservoir_ep07_056.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_056.text: Fu visited after work with a handful of peas too small for the market bowl. She offered them as an ordinary gift from her own supper preparation, not a new household obligation. Yue shelled them while Fu described a quarrel with her brother about the crooked boot knot he had tied. He defended its strength; she objected to its appearance. They agreed that a knot could be sound and still annoy its wearer. Yue wished that her own errors could sometimes be discussed with such a manageable distinction.

reservoir_ep07_057.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_057.text: At the course desk that evening, Yue copied her available private travel money onto a small separate page. The completed grain work had left thirty-seven coppers after the private dispatch and five-day gap. The first course work day had added three. Her original travel contingency remained apart. She would not book a family journey until further real wages and actual road terms supported it. Then she wrote a question for her next letter: would the earlier household visit window still suit her mother if the road opened?

reservoir_ep07_058.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_058.text: She did not send that question yet. The next routine dispatch could include it after the posted work schedule and road reports became firmer. She wanted to avoid turning a wish into an appointment her mother would have to rearrange. Instead she took the plum-tree drawing to the kitchen table and showed it to Jing. Jing said the tree sounded like her father, who had planted beans beyond the bed because the beans apparently preferred his neighbor. Yue laughed and resolved to ask her mother what the wall thought of it.

reservoir_ep07_059.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_059.text: Day One Thousand Eighty-seven brought bright weather and a fresh argument at the basin gate. Two traveling traders wanted to photograph the practice room in their minds and sell its layout as a superior method elsewhere. Qiu offered them the ordinary public receiving explanation and refused entry during candidate preparation. Yue heard their raised voices from the court. The old temptation to settle a room with her own authority flickered. She stayed with her assigned preparation while Qiu, who held the actual gate duty, handled the dispute.

reservoir_ep07_060.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_060.text: The traders eventually bought tea outside and complained to each other. Nothing spectacular had happened. Deng asked Yue to describe what she had missed while listening toward the gate. She had lost the count before her planned release. They began again at the same accepted demand, after she had stopped fully. The incident supplied useful evidence without requiring either trader to become a villain. An ordinary annoyance could disrupt control. If Yue's reservoir depended on everyone outside behaving considerately, it would not remain balanced in the life she already knew.

reservoir_ep07_061.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_061.text: On Day One Thousand Eighty-eight, Yue walked to the footbridge again. The reed still struck the support unevenly. No duck was examining her handwriting today. She had an actual course, a first earned course wage, a repaired hem and a difficult schedule whose dates could not be flattered into different conditions. Downstream, a child dropped a leaf into the current and followed it along the bank. Yue watched the leaf slow in an eddy. Its pause did not mean it had failed to move; the water was still choosing its route.

reservoir_ep07_062.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_062.text: At supper she sat beside the candidate who disliked squash and found the kitchen serving turnips instead. The woman announced a temporary victory over fate. Yue traded half her bread for the last onion slice, then told the swollen-measure story without making herself its central marvel. The other candidate said her own village had a cracked measure nobody wanted to replace because its handle fitted everybody's hand. They planned no universal solution over cold broth. They ate, and Yue carried that practical contradiction with her into the next morning's measured work.

reservoir_ep07_063.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_063.text: Before bed, Yue reread the preregistered criteria once, then closed the paper. She had nearly begun reciting them as a charm against failure. Numbers could guide an examination without protecting her from the day on which they were measured. The low practice room would still contain shutters, noises and her own wish to finish. She extinguished the lamp and lay within the ordinary bedding the course had paid for. Tomorrow Jing would compare the first sample, and Yue would have to live beside its answer.

reservoir_ep07_064.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_064.text: The candidate next door coughed twice and apologized through the thin wall. Yue said the wall had heard worse singing. A muffled laugh followed. Then the room grew quiet, though the basin outside never became silent. Yue did not practice intake in bed to chase a better morning quantity. Deng had told her to arrive rested, and her shoulder agreed with him. She let the familiar circuit settle within its earned stage and attended instead to the relief of having no further task before sleep.

reservoir_ep07_065.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_065.text: At dawn Jing prepared the comparison desk while Deng checked the mat's dry edge. Neither looked excited enough to satisfy the heroic morning Yue had once imagined. Jing was annoyed by a missing ordinary spoon; Deng wanted his tea before it cooled. Their attention belonged to the work they were actually doing. Yue placed her private purse in the room drawer and came to the low seat empty-handed. The first baseline would describe her present reserve, after its real costs, rather than the reserve she hoped to borrow.

reservoir_ep07_066.speaker: narrator
reservoir_ep07_066.text: Outside the pavilion, Tian passed with the basket held firmly against his coat. He waved, then lowered his hand when he saw the prepared instruments. Yue returned a small nod. Their joke could wait until a safer moment. The waiting made it no less theirs. Jing found the spoon beneath a folded cloth, grumbled at herself, and began the blank comparison. Yue watched the empty reference first. She would not make the basin answer before asking what the room had added.
